description: Change-part registry consumed by pipeline_dashboard.html (via /api/registry when served by serve.py, otherwise the embedded copy) and by serve.py. Adding a part type here gives it a Stage 1 schema, Stage 3 branch fields, Stage 4 CadQuery strategy + static checks, sample customer requests and a precedent (RAG) library. Physics validators and 3D/2D geometry live in code — see docs/ADDING_A_PART.md.

starwheel.label: Starwheel
starwheel.summary_for_customer: A rotating wheel with cut-out pockets that carries each container through the capping station.

customer_controls.help: How much room each container has in its pocket. Too snug and containers bind; too loose and they rattle.
A thicker wheel is more rigid and lasts longer, but is heavier to change over.

hotspots.title: Your container sits here
hotspots.body: Each pocket cradles one container as the wheel turns it through the machine.

hotspots.title: Mounts to the machine
hotspots.body: The centre bore fits your machine's shaft.

hotspots.title: Material between pockets
hotspots.body: This band keeps the wheel rigid at speed. We check it never gets too thin.

starwheel.cad_hint: Build a disk of outer diameter OD = pcd_mm + 2*pocket_radius_mm + 2*rim_mm and thickness wheel_thickness_mm, cut a centre bore of bore_diameter_mm, then cut pocket_count circular pockets of radius pocket_radius_mm FULLY THROUGH the disk (cutThruAll) centred on the PCD bolt circle.

starwheel_cap16.label: Starwheel — CAP-16, 16 pockets (reference case)
starwheel_cap16.text:
From: j.hall@brewco.com  Subject: Starwheel quote request

Hi, we need a replacement starwheel for our Morrison CAP-16 capper.
16 pockets, PCD 620mm, bottle diameter 54mm. Target speed 380 CPM.
Material should be UHMW-PE for food contact. Thickness 20mm.

We don't have ovality data for this bottle -- will send later.

starwheel_cap24.label: Starwheel — CAP-24 high-speed line, POM
starwheel_cap24.text:
From: r.delgado@sparklingwave-bev.com  Subject: Need a starwheel for our high-speed line

Hey team,

Our CAP-24 turret needs a new starwheel -- the old one is worn out and
we're seeing early wear on the pocket edges.

Specs: 24 pockets, PCD 900mm, running our round HDPE bottles (thick wall).
Bottle diameter is about 68mm. We push this line at 700 CPM during peak
shifts. Go with POM this time instead of UHMW-PE -- our maintenance lead
wants to try it for the extra stiffness.

Didn't get a chance to measure thickness on the old part, someone will
have to pull the drawing. Let me know what else you need.

Thanks,
Rick

feed_screw.label: Feed Screw (Timing Screw)
feed_screw.summary_for_customer: A rotating screw at the machine infeed whose spiral flight spaces the containers evenly and hands them into the starwheel one at a time.

customer_controls.help: How far apart the screw sets your containers. This has to suit your container diameter.
More flights means the screw turns slower for the same line speed — often the difference between fitting your drive and overspeeding it.
A longer screw controls more containers at once, giving steadier timing.

hotspots.title: The spiral that sets spacing
hotspots.body: As the screw turns, this flight moves each container along by one pitch — that is how they arrive evenly spaced.

hotspots.title: One container per turn
hotspots.body: Containers ride in the gap between flights. We check that gap fits yours even at their widest tolerance.

hotspots.title: Core shaft
hotspots.body: The solid core the flight wraps around. It sets how deeply the flight grips each container.

feed_screw.cad_hint: Build a root cylinder of root_diameter_mm x length_mm. Build ONE flight by sweeping a rectangular profile (radial width (outer_diameter_mm-root_diameter_mm)/2 + 1, thickness flight_thickness_mm, sketched on the XZ plane centred at radius root/2 + (OD-root)/4) along cq.Wire.makeHelix(pitch=pitch_mm*starts, height=length_mm, radius=root_diameter_mm/2) using .sweep(path, isFrenet=True); for starts > 1 union rotated copies of that flight (360/starts degrees apart about Z). Do NOT use twistExtrude - it only rotates the end face and cannot form a multi-turn helix.

feed_screw.label: Feed screw — CAP-16 infeed timing screw
feed_screw.text:
From: m.okafor@northridgebottling.com  Subject: Infeed timing screw for line 3 filler

Hi -- we need a new infeed feed screw for the Morrison CAP-16 on line 3.
Bottle is a 66mm diameter round PET, and we run the line at 380 CPM.
The screw needs to be about 480mm long, right-hand, in UHMW-PE.
For pitch and outside diameter use whatever suits the bottle -- the old
drawing is lost, so please propose them and tell us why.

Thanks, Maya

feed_screw_glass.label: Feed screw — CAP-16, 750 ml glass, POM, left-hand
feed_screw_glass.text:
From: t.brennan@ridgelinespirits.ie  Subject: Timing screw for the new 750 ml line

Hi,

We're adding a Morrison CAP-16 filler/capper on the 750 ml line and need
an infeed timing screw for it. The bottle is round glass, 84 mm diameter,
about 300 mm tall. We want to run it at 420 CPM.

The screw has to fit a 600 mm long infeed section. Please make it in POM --
our glass bottles chew up UHMW too quickly. Left-hand rotation to match
the conveyor.

We'd like your recommendation on pitch, diameter and number of starts;
we don't have a drawing for this one.

Cheers,
Tom

guide_rail.label: Guide Rail
guide_rail.summary_for_customer: A curved rail that runs around part of the starwheel and keeps each container seated in its pocket while it is carried round.

customer_controls.help: A longer wrap supports containers for more of the turn, but past 180° it blocks access when you change over.
How close the rail sits to your containers. Too close pinches them, too far lets them tip out of the pocket.
Where the rail touches the container. It should press on the straight body, not the shoulder or the base.

hotspots.title: Guides the container
hotspots.body: This face runs alongside your containers and keeps them seated in the starwheel pockets.

hotspots.title: Your containers
hotspots.body: Shown to scale so you can see the running gap between them and the rail.

hotspots.title: The starwheel it works with
hotspots.body: The rail curves to match the wheel this part runs against.

guide_rail.cad_hint: Sketch an annular sector on the XY plane: inner arc of radius rail_radius_mm and outer arc of rail_radius_mm + thickness_mm spanning arc_angle_deg (moveTo / threePointArc / lineTo / threePointArc / close), then extrude by rail_height_mm.

guide_rail.label: Guide rail — CAP-16 discharge outer rail
guide_rail.text:
From: s.lindqvist@fjordwater.se  Subject: Replacement outer guide rail, capper discharge

Hello,
The outer guide rail on our CAP-16 discharge starwheel (PCD 620mm) is cracked.
Our bottle is 54mm diameter, 210mm tall, round PET, and the line runs 380 CPM.
The rail should wrap about 120 degrees around the wheel, 25mm high and 12mm
thick, in UHMW-PE. Contact height about 95mm above the conveyor -- that is on
the label panel of the bottle.
Regards, Sara

guide_rail_cap24.label: Guide rail — CAP-24 discharge, HDPE, 150° wrap
guide_rail_cap24.text:
From: k.nakamura@hokusei-drinks.jp  Subject: Outer guide rail, CAP-24 discharge side

Hello,

We need a replacement outer guide rail for the discharge starwheel on our
Morrison CAP-24. The starwheel PCD is 900 mm. Our container is a 68 mm
round HDPE bottle, 245 mm tall, and the line runs at 700 CPM.

The old rail wrapped 150 degrees around the wheel and was 30 mm high,
12 mm thick, in POM. Contact height was 110 mm above the conveyor.

Please confirm the rail radius and let us know if 150 degrees is still OK.

Best regards,
Kenji Nakamura
